title: Discount From the Next Cheaper Price
statement:
A shop lists items in a row with prices prices. Each item gets a discount: find the first item to its right whose price is less than or equal to its own, and subtract that item's price. If no such item exists, there is no discount.

Return an array with the final price of every item, in the original order.

examples.why: 9 takes 4 off (first cheaper item), 4 and 6 both take 2 off. 2 and 3 have nothing cheaper to their right.
An equal price counts. The last item has nobody to its right.
The discount for 7 is not the 8 next to it: it is the first price that is not higher, the 3.

hints: The direct way scans right from every item. When is that slow?
Items still waiting for a discount always form a sequence of strictly rising prices. Why?
Keep a stack of indexes still waiting. When a new price arrives, it is the discount for every waiting item whose price is at least as high: pop them and settle them, then push the new index.

explain.intuition:
Scanning right from each item is O(n²) when prices keep rising, because nobody finds a cheaper item for a long time. Flip it around: walk left to right and let each new price settle the older items that were waiting for it.

Keep a stack of indexes whose discount is still unknown. When price p arrives, every waiting item with price ≥ p has just found its first cheaper-or-equal item, so pop and settle them. The ones left are cheaper than p and keep waiting. That is why the stack always holds strictly rising prices, and each index is pushed and popped once.
steps: Copy prices into result and start with an empty stack of indexes.
For each index i, while the stack is not empty and prices[top] ≥ prices[i], pop top and set result[top] −= prices[i].
Indexes left on the stack get no discount. Return result.
pitfalls: Using strictly less than. An equal price also counts as the discount, as in [5, 5, 5].
Taking the cheapest item to the right instead of the first one that is not more expensive.
Subtracting the discount from prices itself while the stack still compares against it. Write into a separate result array.

solutions.title: Scan right from every item
solutions.idea: For each item, walk right until the first price that is not higher.

solutions.title: Monotonic stack of waiting items
solutions.idea: Each new price settles every waiting item that is at least as expensive. What stays waiting forms a rising stack.

followups: The discount comes from the first cheaper item to the left instead. What changes?
Prices arrive as a stream and you must report each item's final price as soon as it is known. Does the stack still work?
